purpose: index-then-curve mismatch fix: settings.json enabled weekly_rsi=0.25/weekly_macd=0.5 (commit 82cd1ddcc) but the currently-published curve (btc_curve_optimize_provenance.json / btc_optimized_provenance.json) was fit against a stale 3-member index (valuation+m2+dxy only, from a divergent branch, commit 4dece6542). This file re-fits the curve on the actually-live 5-member index and walk-forward-validates it.

walk_forward.data_source_note: BTC-USD.csv refreshed via `digiquant prices preload-history --tickers BTC-USD --years 12` (yfinance) to cover 2014-09-17→2026-09-02; the previously cached CSV only went back to 2017-01-01 and could not satisfy fit_btc_power_law's 730-day-per-fold minimum. Values differ slightly from the Coinbase-sourced cache used in older provenance files (different vendor), directionally consistent.

fold_scores.note: CORRECTED 2026-10-17 (endpoint-metric fix): fold 2 in-sample capital_deployed_pct = -2558% is NOT short-side accounting. It is the documented end-of-window cash snapshot, (initial_cash - cash)/initial_cash*100 (backtest.py::SdcaBacktestReport.capital_deployed_pct). No short position is possible -- size_trade clamps every sell to units held -- so the figure only goes negative because the curve sold appreciated BTC into the 2021 top and ended holding far more cash than the initial stake. The book fully participated (capital_deployed_peak_pct ~100%). Reproduced on the real fold-2 window (2014-09-17->2021-11-20, power-law rails, published cycle-4 curve): capital_deployed_pct = -19402%, peak = 100.0%, min(asset_units) = 0, min(cash) = 0. Gate feasibility on the peak, not this snapshot; this fold's vs-flat figures are unaffected.

notes: Mismatch confirmed via commit ancestry (not raw timestamps -- 82cd1ddcc and 4dece6542 are on divergent branches, so timestamp order is meaningless; content + ancestor check is what settles it).

curve_simulator and Nautilus sharply disagree for this candidate: curve_simulator says +314.5% vs-flat in-sample, Nautilus says -13.8% vs-flat in-sample for the identical params. Do not average or reconcile these -- AGENTS.md's 'one evaluator per question' rule is exactly why this file reports both separately instead of picking one.

Sensitivity is unstable (max_abs_delta_oos_pct=36.79 vs a 2.0 threshold): a 5% perturbation of the winning shape swings OOS by up to ~37 points. The curve_simulator winner is fragile under Nautilus even setting aside the failing OOS sign.

settings.json / presets.json / btc_optimized_provenance.json / btc_curve_optimize_provenance.json are intentionally left untouched -- this trial is not a chosen candidate, so nothing is persisted or published. The live preset still runs the old (index-mismatched) curve pending a decision on how to proceed.
